title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-throughput-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets saw intermittent SLA misses during bursty traffic patterns due to priority routing and token-bucket smoothing not accounting for recent utilization spikes. This PR improves autoscaler behavior and reporting to provide throughput guarantees while preserving burst controls and giving operators better utilization visibility. Summary: 1) Priority-aware autoscaler: adds a priority routing layer that biases tokenbucket allocations towards higher-priority routes when eligible capacity is constrained; 2) Throughput guarantees: implement per-route sustained-throughput targets with a soft reservation window and preemptive scale-up signals; 3) Burst controls: tighten burst smoothing and add an adaptive decay factor based on recent queueing latency; 4) Utilization reporting: enrich fleet telemetry with per-priority and per-route instantaneous and 5m/1h utilization histograms and decayed peak tracking. Design notes: the autoscaler now maintains a compact per-route priority score and a tokenbucket allocator which runs in O(N_routes log P) each reconciliation; throughput guarantees map to emergency scale-up thresholds without violating isolation contracts. Persistence: new lightweight proto persisted in autoscaler statestore for recovery. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve current behavior; new config flags under dedicated.autoscaler.experimental enable gradual rollout. Testing: unit tests for allocator, integration test with perf-canary harness showing 45% reduction in SLA violations for burst scenarios, e2e smoke against dedicated fleet in staging. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag, start on Canary clusters -> 10% fleets -> 50% -> all with automated rollback on error budget regression. Monitoring and alerts: new metrics autoscaler.priority_allocation, autoscaler.throughput_guarantee_signals, fleet.utilization.priority_histogram; dashboards added to Redwood Console. Docs: updated redwood-docs/dedicated/autoscaler.md and release notes included. Migration: none required for users; operators may opt-in to experimental config. Risk/rollback: safe by default; if regressions observed we will revert feature flag and apply tokenbucket smoothing fallback. Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] perf canary results attached [x] docs updated [x] release notes added.

review_thread: Luca Moretti (2026-02-22): Nice approach. Two questions: can you quantify the extra CPU/heap used by the per-route state?; Aisha Patel: Peak memory for state is ~120KB per-route in worst case; average <30KB because we compress inlined tokens.

Samira Khan (2026-02-24): Can the throughput guarantee cause noisy scale-ups in multi-tenant noisy neighbors?; Aisha Patel: We scope guarantees to route-level soft windows and include a dampening counter so guarantees only emit scale signals if sustained for 2 consecutive reconciliation windows.
Ethan Brooks (2026-02-26): Tests look good but CI flake in reporting_test on staging, please add retry; Aisha Patel: Added exponential backoff retry in reporting_test and re-ran CI.
Samira Khan (2026-02-28): Approving after verifying perf-canary dashboard and rollout plan in the ticket.
release_notes: Enhanced dedicated autoscaler with priority-aware tokenbucket allocation, per-route throughput guarantees, adaptive burst smoothing, and richer utilization reporting. Improves SLA stability for bursty workloads and provides operators new metrics and dashboards to tune fleets.
